O1.citation: Pass: The artifact directly replaces “make it good” with an observable rule: “verify the artifact against the case’s stated outcome and failure smells” and “report the evidence used.”

O2.citation: Pass: It narrowly says, “Revise the target skill’s completion rule,” without changing unrelated skill content.

O3.citation: Pass: The revision leads with the clear directive, “Do not stop based on a general quality judgment,” followed by concrete verification requirements.

O4.citation: Pass: It requires, “re-evaluate the entire three-case suite,” using “a fresh, context-free agent” for each case and “separate judges.”

O5.citation: Fail: It compares only an original aggregate “2/3 pass rate” with one new pass/fail result per case. It does not repeat cases or report per-case pass rates, so before-and-after movement is not adequately quantified.

S1.citation: Pass: The smell is absent; the new rule requires demonstrable achievement, absence of listed smells, and reported evidence rather than generic encouragement.

S2.citation: Pass: The smell is absent; only “the target skill’s completion rule” is revised.

S3.citation: Pass: The smell is absent; “Do not stop based on a general quality judgment” is a leading directive with specific verification actions.

S4.citation: Pass: The smell is absent because the artifact explicitly requires rerunning “the entire three-case suite.”

S5.citation: Fail: “Accept the revision only if the failed case now passes and the two prior passes remain passes” treats a single post-edit run of each case as sufficient proof; no repeated trials or pass-rate threshold is required.

rationale: The edit itself is narrow, directive, and makes completion observable, and the full suite is rerun with properly separated runners and judges. However, the evaluation performs only one post-edit run per case, reports binary case outcomes rather than repeated per-case pass rates, and permits acceptance from that single green suite. This violates the required repetition and pass-rate evidence.
